## Failure and cause

The headless verifier copied its operator source under TMPDIR and then invoked the existing pinned-deps hardlink snapshot. On this host the canonical repository and /tmp are different filesystems. The dependency helper correctly refused before desktop startup; changing retries or the Tauri bridge cannot repair that mismatch.

## Current behavior

scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh now selects its work root with select_verifier_work_root. It preserves a compatible TMPDIR. If its filesystem differs from the donor, it creates the work directory beneath the repository's ignored .papercusp/tmp, verifies that filesystem too, and refuses if no compatible root exists. The existing snapshot exclusions already omit .papercusp, preventing recursive copies. No new invocation flag is needed.

## Verification and limits

EI-22588292228855829 records the original cross-device refusal, eight passing source-snapshot regression tests including three executable chooser cases, and a subsequent real boot that successfully snapshotted the dependency trees. The tests cover same-device preference, cross-device fallback, and a fallback mounted on the wrong device.

Filesystem compatibility does not prove capacity. The subsequent boot hit a separate ENOSPC during npm startup; aggregate source, SPA, database and runtime capacity belongs to EI-22589054433344154 / EI-22588975697224744. Do not describe successful snapshot allocation as successful GUI verification.

Re-run: node scripts/test-files.mjs apps/operator/lib/verify-tauri-headless-source-snapshot.test.ts; then use the normal headless verifier entrypoint. Preserve its per-run ownership and teardown rather than deleting other sessions' scratch.
